headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: A month of steep losses; the last weeks lean clearly down

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 9% in a week and about 27% in a month, and a Rally watch drop window has been open since 11 November. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and step up acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,379) and then the 200-day average ($72,322). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is near $59,490 and fear is extreme, so today is about calm, safety and holding steady, not promotions. Short term, the picture is weak: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 32 days in a row, sits about 22% below it and about 27% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 11 out of 100. News is pulling this lower, as Nvidia fell 14% in a single day and the Nasdaq dropped about 5% (PANews), dragging risky assets with it. A normal week lately swings about $3,988, so a close above $61,500 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would turn it down further, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit far better than offers right now.

The next month leans down: price is about 27% lower than 30 days ago and about 25% lower than 90 days ago, and the medium-term reading has been in its weak zone for two days in a row, though the model needs five in a row before the headline switches from NEUTRAL to BEARISH. On the other side, Abraxas Capital bought about $897 million of Bitcoin into the drop and Morgan Stanley added about 800 BTC (both PANews), a sign some large buyers are still adding. Bitcoin would have to win back $76,646 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only barely: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), yet price is about 18% under it, about 13% under its 200-week average and about 52% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,322 (the 200-day average) again; $68,379 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped well under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. More weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users rather than winning new ones.

items.theme: Prediction markets under legal pressure while they grow
items.why: PANews reports 44 US state attorneys general oppose the CFTC's prediction-market rulemaking, and a New York court will hear a request on 24 November to bar Kalshi from the state, which Kalshi says would shut its whole US business. At the same time Bloomberg (via PANews) says some crypto investors are moving money into prediction markets, and Fortune reports Kalshi's institutional volume rose to $26.3 billion in October.

items.theme: A run of hacks and exchange glitches
